subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Smart Glass: Windows That Think
description: A quick win: understand Smart Glass: Windows That Think.

hook.text: Electrochromic glass changes from clear to opaque with a small electrical charge. No blinds, no curtains — just smart glass.

buildup.text: A thin coating of tungsten oxide is sandwiched between glass layers. When voltage is applied, ions migrate and the glass darkens.

discovery.text: Smart glass reduces cooling costs by 25% in commercial buildings. It blocks solar heat gain while maintaining daylight views.

twist.text: Boeing's 787 uses electrochromic windows instead of plastic shades. Passengers dim them with a button — no more shade battles.

climax.text: Future smart glass could generate solar power while controlling light. Transparent solar cells in glass are in development.

punchline.text: Apply voltage. Glass darkens. Remove voltage. Glass clears. No moving parts.

quiz.question: How does electrochromic smart glass change from clear to dark?
options: Liquid crystals between glass layers rotate to block or transmit light
An electrical charge moves ions through a tungsten oxide coating, darkening it
A thin film of mercury vapor condenses on the inner surface when heated
